name: Resonance
description: Breathe at the body's natural resonant frequency, about 5.5 breaths per minute. This pace maximizes heart rate variability and settles the heart and lungs into one steady rhythm.

name: Deep Calm
description: An ultra-slow rhythm of 3.75 breaths per minute that shifts the nervous system into its lowest gear. For deep relaxation and recovery.
Dr. Andrew Weil's pattern for winding down. The 7-second hold lets oxygen saturate the blood, and the long exhale slows the heart. Often used to fall asleep faster.

name: Box
description: Equal inhale, hold, exhale, and hold. A balanced rhythm for staying calm and focused under pressure. Scale the duration to what you can sustain: 3s per phase to start, 5 to 6s if moderate, 8 to 10s if seasoned.

name: Extended Exhale
description: A 1:2 inhale-to-exhale ratio. The long exhale stimulates the vagus nerve and tips the body toward rest and digest. One of the simplest ways to calm down.
Inhale for 7, exhale for 11. The much longer exhale at a slow pace makes this one of the strongest simple relaxation patterns there is.

name: Physiological Sigh
description: A double inhale followed by a long exhale. The second sip of air reopens collapsed air sacs in the lungs, so a single cycle can release real tension. Use one to three breaths as a quick reset when stress spikes.

name: Increasing Breaths
description: Each round stretches slightly longer than the last, training the body to slow down and deepen its natural rhythm.

name: Breathe Light
description: Patrick McKeown's core Oxygen Advantage exercise. Reduce your breathing volume until you feel a tolerable air hunger, which trains the body to deliver oxygen more efficiently. Breathe so quietly that the fine hairs in your nostrils barely move.

name: Breath of Fire
description: Rapid, rhythmic breathing from Kundalini yoga. Builds energy, increases alertness, and strengthens the diaphragm through sustained diaphragmatic pumping followed by a long retention that concentrates the energizing effect.

name: Bellow Breathing
description: Rapid double-inhale and exhale cycles that ramp in intensity, followed by a deep inhale and an extended hold that grows longer each round. A progressive engine that builds heat and energy.

name: Brown Fat Activation
description: Strong, forceful inhales and breath holds meant to stimulate brown fat, the tissue that burns energy to make heat. The inhale-heavy ratio (3.5s in, 1.5s out) adds a stimulating charge.

name: Timed Tummo
description: A Tibetan inner heat practice. Vigorous inhale-heavy breathing followed by long holds builds warmth and focus. Traditionally practiced in freezing conditions.

name: Wim Hof
description: The Wim Hof Method: rounds of strong, fast breathing, then a hold on empty lungs, then a recovery breath with a short hold. Expect tingling, lightness, and a clear-headed lift afterward.

name: CO₂ Tolerance
description: Gradually lengthens the exhale across three stages to train your tolerance to carbon dioxide, the main trigger of the urge to breathe. Improves breath holds and everyday breathing efficiency.

name: Apnea
description: Breath hold training with progressively longer retention times. Builds comfort with air hunger and trains the dive reflex for freediving and general breath control.

name: Retention
description: Simple breath retention practice with holds after each exhale. An accessible entry point to breath-hold training that builds CO₂ tolerance and calms the mind.

name: CO₂ Table
description: The standard freediving CO₂ table: hold length stays the same while the rests shrink each round, training the brain to tolerate rising carbon dioxide. Eight rounds, increasingly uncomfortable.

name: O₂ Table
description: The companion freediving O₂ table: rests stay the same while the holds grow each round, training the body to run on less oxygen and extending breath-hold capacity.

name: Shamanic
description: Progressive box breathing with increasing durations and extended holds between rounds. A meditative journey that deepens with each cycle, building from 4-count to 8-count box patterns.

name: Altered State
description: Intense, rhythmic overbreathing followed by a long hold, reaching for a meditative altered state. The fast breathing depletes CO₂, and the hold that follows is where the shift happens.

name: Dopamine Light
description: An accelerating pattern that builds intensity through progressively faster cycles, ending in a long hold. Made to lift mood and energy.

name: Holotropic
description: Based on Stanislav Grof's holotropic breathwork. Sustained deep, fast breathing that accelerates as it goes, pushing toward expanded states of awareness, with an open-ended hold at the end.

name: Slow Drift
description: A 30-minute trance induction through ultra-slow breathing. No intensity, just a steady rhythm slow enough to quiet the wandering mind. The breath lengthens gently over the first 10 minutes, then holds you there.

name: Cultivation
description: A daily energy practice rooted in Qigong and pranayama. Slow nasal breathing with a gentle hold after each inhale accumulates energy like filling a reservoir. No intensity, no discomfort, just a steady charge that builds over weeks of practice.

name: Nadi Shodhana
description: Alternate nostril breathing in the classical 1:2:2 pranayama ratio. Switching airflow between nostrils balances the nervous system and steadies the mind.

seq.text: Close your right nostril. Breathe through the left
Switch. Close your left nostril. Breathe through the right

name: Bhramari
description: The humming bee breath. A continuous hum through the exhale vibrates the airways, stimulates the vagus nerve, and boosts nasal nitric oxide. Deeply calming.

seq.text: Close ears with thumbs. Hum on exhale, mouth closed, teeth slightly apart
Release your ears. Sit still and listen to the fading resonance

name: Sitali
description: Inhaling across a curled tongue cools the body and settles the mind. One of the few pranayamas that deliberately uses mouth inhalation.

seq.text: Curl tongue edges upward to form a tube. Inhale through tongue like sipping a straw
Close mouth. Return to normal nasal breathing

name: Viloma
description: Interrupted breathing developed by B.K.S. Iyengar. The inhale is split into three segments with short pauses between them, like filling a glass from bottom to top. Expands lung capacity and teaches precise control.

name: Sniper Breathing
description: A two-phase protocol from marksmanship training: box breathing to settle the nervous system, then working the natural pause at the bottom of the exhale, the few seconds where the body is stillest. Built for precision.

name: SOMA Awakening
description: A multi-phase protocol combining rhythmic breathing, exhale retention, and inhale retention with body locks. Reaches for bliss and expanded awareness.

name: Hook Recovery
description: The recovery technique freedivers and fighter pilots use after a breath hold. A sharp inhale and a brief pressure hold push oxygen into the blood and up to the brain much faster than passive breathing. Use it after any apnea exercise.

name: Awakened Nap
description: A 20-minute wind-down toward sleep. Begins at resonance pace, then lengthens the exhale to settle the nervous system before shortening each cycle into the shallow rhythms of drift.
